verdict.rationale: Sill is a remote-desktop tool, so a shared address book or console with per-group access policies is a fair question to ask of it. The evidence shows no such capability. Each Mac only keeps its own local list of paired devices, and Sill explicitly has no account and no server, so there is nothing to host a shared, group-policy-managed directory.

support.subject: As an IT admin, machines and users are organized in a shared address book or console with per-group access policies
